```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is one paying customer within 90 days. B carries a much lighter regulatory load than A. B needs GDPR/CCPA privacy review and a standard ToS/SLA template. A needs COPPA verifiable parental consent, consent-record and deletion processes, and unspecified state-level children's privacy laws before any launch.",
    "B's build scope is narrow and concrete: incidents, components, subscriber emails and a public page. A's MVP needs adaptive content across reading, writing and arithmetic plus speech recognition, and its pedagogy faces public efficacy scrutiny.",
    "B has a sourced proof that a single operator can earn real revenue in the category: Instatus at ~$10k MRR (Starter Story). A has no sourced example of a solo operator reaching revenue.",
    "B's buyers are businesses with sourced complaints about incumbent pricing, such as the r/SaaS thread on paying $399/month for a manually updated page. These buyers are reachable in channels where a solo builder already operates (Indie Hackers, Product Hunt, dev SEO). A's main zero-spend channel is unproven, and A's own brief says child-product trust builds over months, not a six-week sales cycle.",
    "B gets its first-customer edge from regulatory and trust-cycle factors, not from weaker competition. Both ideas face free, capable incumbents: OneUptime for B, and Khan Academy Kids and Samio for A.",
    "A's strongest demand quote cuts against it. The Mentava review quote is a parent deciding not to pay, which shows price resistance rather than willingness to pay."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's main low-cost acquisition channel, organic parenting communities on Reddit, is explicitly marked [unsourced cost], and its reach and conversion are stated as unproven. A's Case For also relies on 'parents pay tutors $25-$120/hour (per multiple tutoring-cost sources)', which cites no URL and so counts as missing. Without a credible channel, A has no evidenced path to a first paying parent at a sub-$15/month price, where the brief says paid UA is hard to justify economically.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe saturated markets anchored by free alternatives, and both lack evidence of a differentiated wedge. B's case also has a soft spot: the Instatus figure of '~$500/mo MRR growth after years' implies slow economics. B wins mainly because it has fewer launch blockers (regulation, child-trust cycles) for reaching a single paying customer in 90 days, not because its demand evidence is clearly stronger."
}
```
